newsitem.title: THAILAND: NAP seen winner by slim majority in Thai poll.
newsitem.headline: NAP seen winner by slim majority in Thai poll.

text.p: Thailand's New Aspiration Party (NAP) headed by outgoing Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh looked poised to win general elections on Sunday by the narrowest of majorities, local media reported.
The main Channel 9 television station said the NAP was projected to win 125 of the 393 seats in parliament against 123 for the Democrat Party of former premier Chuan Leekpai.
Chavalit, attending a news conference along with leaders of four other allied political parties, told a news conference he sensed victory.
"We are here together to show that we are victorious...but we should be patient, taking one step at a time," he said.
The party leaders were appearing together in order to show they were prepared to work together in the future, although no definite decision had been made to forge a coalition, he added.
One of the party leaders at the news conference forecast that the five parties together were set to control over 200 of the 393 seats in parliament. Official results are expected early on Monday.
Political commentators said it looked likely the NAP could form thte core of a new coalition government.
Democrat leader Chuan acknowledged unofficial reports that the NAP was slightly ahead in television projections.

"According to the information that I have followed, the Democrat Party has not emerged as the number one party and therefore we will be in the opposition in the future...if the reports prove to be correct," he told reporters in his southern hometown in Trang.
Among party leaders who gathered with Chavalit was outgoing premier Banharn Silpa-archa, who heads the Chart Thai party, projected to win about 40 seats, and leaders of three other smaller parties.
Another smaller party, the Chart Pattana party led by former premier Chatichai Choonhavan which is projected to win over 50 seats, was reported to be allied to the Democrats.
Smaller parties were expected to play key roles in the formation of any new coalition government as the NAP and Democrats sought to secure a majority in parliament, analysts said.
This election, the fourth in as many years, was billed as the dirtiest and most violent in two decades.

The independent election watchdog Pollwatch said seven people had been killed in violence before election day and up to 30 billion baht ($1.2 billion) spent by politicians, some of it on buying votes.
